title: Write review 2 re-checking the revised squash-chain landing design
summary: I read "re-check" as asking for a second independent review (review 2) of the revised docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md. It would confirm that each review-1 finding was answered and that the revised claims match the code and D69. This follows the review-2 precedent for the athena-v0 and study-capability-m1 designs.

defaults_applied.how: Recovered the target (revised design) and the form (review 2) from the repo's review-1 file and earlier review-2 precedents.
The review cites sections and code line numbers and labels unmeasured claims.
One new review document plus a changelog line.
No personal data or secrets in the review.
Written for an outside reader with stable finding ids.

assumptions: 'Re-check' means write an independent review-2 document, as was done for athena-v0 and study-capability-m1, rather than edit the design.
The design at HEAD is the revised version (it has a response appendix to review 1 and D69 mentions athena.candidate/2).
The re-check does not run code; it reads, as review 1 did.
CHANGELOG.md gets one line recording the review, as earlier reviews did.

acceptance_criteria.text: New file docs/design/reviews/squash-chain-landing-review-2.md exists, in the format of study-capability-m1-review-2.md: verdict, severity scale, stable finding ids (R2-...), and a 'what this review read and ran' section.

Every review-1 finding (R1-M1..M3, R1-m1..m5, R1-n1..n2) and its three decisions for the user is checked against the revised design's response appendix (around line 271) and its stated disposition is confirmed, disputed, or marked unchecked, each with a cited section or code line.

The revised design's new claims about code (invariant.rs, jobs.rs, history.rs, records.rs, attrs.rs) are re-checked against the current code, with line numbers, and mismatches are reported as findings.

Check that D69 in docs/decisions.md and the pointers in docs/enforcement.md, docs/architecture.md and athena-v0.md agree with the revised design (e.g. schema athena.candidate/2, merge commits, rule-changing chains).
The review claims only what it read; any number is measured or labelled as an estimate; no secrets or personal data appear.
Run `cargo test --locked`; it passes, including the repository's wording scan over docs. Run `cargo fmt --check`; it is clean.
No Rust code, governance file, the design itself, or anything under records/ is changed (design edits only if the review's findings are explicitly applied, which is out of scope here).

out_of_scope: Implementing chain landing in Rust (the build follow-up).
Editing the design to apply review findings.
Changing athena.toml, [history] exempt entries, or any governance file.
departures: Slightly higher cost than the reference: the review must read a long design, review 1, and several source files.
